brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.

requirements.requirement: Herb planter of three cells side by side (three hex cells in a row)
requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases (piece) at cells (-1,0), (0,0), (1,0) in a straight row, locked with two joint bolts (jointBolt 0#0,0#3 and 0#1,0#3 plus one more on the (-1,0)-(0,0) wall). check_build meshClash clear, no LOOSE_BODY left.

requirements.requirement: Each of the three cells holds a bin that drains (drained bin)
requirements.evidence: Three hex-bin-full-drain bins, one in each base at (-1,0), (0,0), (1,0); BOM shows Bin, full depth, drained qty 3.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell row of full hex bases with a drained full-depth bin in each cell, joint-bolted together. check_build is clean (meshClash clear, no errors). No soil or herbs were added; the brief reads as the planter structure, so I left dressing out. Note the BOM's PETG torque guidance: hand-tighten the M6 bolts to about 2 N.m.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
